# The letters

After stating its system in brief, the 1446 book explained the letters one
class at a time: the initial consonants, the vowels, the final consonants.
Each class was explained by the same method.

This part does the same for gog's letters. The marks are the consonants:
visible forms that draw nothing until a position says where they go. The positions are the vowels: `x`, `y`, and `z`, plus the scales
that decide how a number, a category, or a date becomes a place on an
axis. The refining channels are the finals: `color`, `size`, `shape`,
`pattern`, `opacity`. Each is optional, and each earns the legend that
decodes it. `group` sits outside both classes: it splits a mark without
encoding anything, so it earns no legend, and it works like the space
between words. `label` and `play` stand outside the syllable too: one
supplies a `text` mark's words, and the other cuts the plot into frames
and plays them in order. `play` acts on the whole plot, the way faceting
does, so its chapter waits in the next part.
Around the letters sit the chapters that complete a layer.
[Data](../data.qmd), the table you bind once, opens this part, because
nothing can be drawn until a table is named. [The book's
data](../book-data.qmd) follows, saying where this book's own tables come
from and how to read one in your language. [Setting vs mapping](../style.qmd) draws the line between a column you
*map* and a constant you *set*, and [Transforms](../transforms.qmd), which
derives new values from your columns, closes the part.

Each mark has a chapter of its own, fourteen in a row from
[point](../marks/point.qmd) to [edge](../marks/edge.qmd), and every one
follows the same template: what it draws, what it requires, what refines
it, what derives from it, what you can set on it, and what it refuses. The last two are always the last two, under those names. That
sameness is deliberate: it is the No Exceptions law applied to a book's
structure, and it means learning the second mark is faster than the first,
and by the fifth mark you already know the shape.
